data.title: Nvidia-backed neocloud Nscale files for IPO
data.description:
The U.K-based neocloud provider Nscale filed its initial public offering prospectus with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on Friday.

The company applied to appear on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker NSCL. The filing did not include an expected price range or the number of stocks to be offered. Goldman Sachs (GS), J.P. Morgan (JPM) and Morgan Stanley (MS) will act as lead bookrunners for the proposed offering.

Nscale has data centers in the U.K., Norway and Texas, with several more partner-run data centers operating in Europe and the U.S. 

"We serve some of the largest companies on Earth through strategic partnerships and long-term agreements," Nscale founder and CEO Josh Payne noted in the filing. "This is the foundation that funds the continued buildout of our global footprint, and we believe the opportunity ahead here is vast. With a 10 GW+ portfolio of owned and controlled power, we expect significant expansion in Nscale Infrastructure as we grow with our existing customers, and contract and scale new customers building and delivering frontier intelligence."

As of August 31, 2026, the company's infrastructure portfolio included about 25,000 active GPUs and 461,000 active and contracted GPUs, along with five active and 12 contracted data center sites. What's more, the company had $2.6B of active and $103.4B of active and contracted TCV under long-term take-or-pay contracts with customers, compared to $500M of active and $38B of active and contracted TCV at the end of 2025. Nscale relies almost exclusively on Nvidia (NVDA) GPUs. The company has signifcant contracts with Microsoft (MSFT) and Anthropic (ANTHRO).

Revenue for the first six months of 2026 totaled $140.6M, compared to $10.4M during the same period in 2025. The company also incurred a net loss of $1.02B for the first six months of 2026 due to substantial investments the company has made to grow its platform.

data.title: Trump to 'demand' vaccine makers make smaller doses for kids to address autism
data.description:
• President Trump on Friday told reporters in the Oval Office that he will "demand" that companies that make childhood vaccines manufacture doses that are significantly smaller than currently recommended to cut autism rates. 
  • Speaking at a press conference about expanding "Most Favored Nation" drug pricing to Medicaid recipients in all states, Trump said a recommendation will be made to give childhood vaccines through five shots spaced six-months apart.
  • The president noted that the change would lead to a “massive reduction” in autism cases.
  • Prominent scientific organizations, citing studies, have repeatedly stated that there is no relationship between vaccines and autism. "This has been confirmed through dozens of scientific studies examining different types of vaccines and different vaccine timing schedules," the Autism Science Foundation says.  
  • HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has been a long-time skeptic of vaccines and has not rejected the vaccines-autism link.
  • In August, Trump signed an executive order that significantly impacts the childhood vaccines schedule, including that the immunizations should be done at multiple medical visits.

data.title: Saratoga Investment CFO steps down for health reasons
data.description:
Saratoga Investments (SAR) Chief Financial Officer Henri Steenkamp will step down from that role  as of Oct. 31, 2026, for health-related reasons, the company said on Friday.

He'll also relinquish his roles as chief compliance officer, treasurer, and secretary on that same date. Steenkamp will continue to serve in a consulting capacity following the transition. He will remain on the company's board and will serve as the CFO of the company's SBIC subsidiaries.

Also effective Oct. 31, 2026, Saratoga Investments (SAR) will promote:

  • Christine Ramdihal to chief accounting officer and treasurer and will serve as the company's principal financial officer.
  • Rochelle Kracoff to chief compliance officer and secretary.
  • James Soltesz to investment manager and vice president of Capital Markets.

Saratoga Investment (SAR) stock edged down 0.2% in after-hours trading.

data.title: Anthropic advances IPO plans as AI safety debate intensifies
data.description:
Anthropic is moving forward with preparations for a potentially major initial public offering, even as its chief executive, Dario Amodei, has called for stronger safeguards and a slower pace of development for some advanced artificial intelligence systems, according to reporting by The New York Times.

The AI company, which develops the Claude chatbot, is projected to generate more than $100B in annualized revenue this year, according to people familiar with its finances cited by the Times. That figure would represent a significant increase from the roughly $65B annualized revenue reported in July.

The strong growth has fueled expectations among investors that Anthropic could command a valuation of as much as $2 trillion in a public offering. According to people familiar with the company's plans, Anthropic could file financial documents related to the IPO in the coming weeks, potentially allowing its shares to begin trading as early as November. 

The potential IPO comes as the AI industry faces growing scrutiny over the risks posed by increasingly powerful models. Amodei has recently advocated additional safeguards around AI development, adding to an ongoing debate over how quickly the technology should advance.

Going public would provide Anthropic with access to substantial amounts of capital at a time when the company faces enormous computing expenses. Investors expect Anthropic to have access to about five gigawatts of computing capacity by the end of this year and potentially double that amount by the end of 2027, according to people familiar with the figures. Such capacity would place it broadly alongside rival OpenAI.

Anthropic has also been actively engaging with potential investors. The company recently hosted roughly 100 venture capital investors at its San Francisco headquarters for an event focused on its technology and products. Several Anthropic executives and co-founders participated, along with AI researcher Andrej Karpathy, who joined the company this year after previously co-founding OpenAI.

During meetings with prospective investors, Anthropic has emphasized potential benefits of AI, including applications in biology and medical research. The company has also sought to reassure investors about competition from lower-cost, open-weight AI models developed in China, arguing that only a relatively small share of businesses currently depend on those systems, according to the Times' sources.

Some investors believe Anthropic can continue expanding even if it slows development in certain areas. Much of its revenue comes from businesses using Claude, and corporate adoption of generative AI remains at an early stage.

At the same time, the IPO could present unusual challenges. Lawyers and bankers cited by the Times said Anthropic is entering largely unfamiliar territory because of the potential legal and financial consequences associated with advanced AI systems. Questions have also been raised about how the company could balance AI safety objectives with the growth expectations that typically accompany being a publicly traded company.

Anthropic's governance structure could provide some protection for its safety-focused mission, but going public would bring greater financial disclosure and scrutiny.

The company's plans also contrast with those of OpenAI. The Times reported that OpenAI's chief executive, Sam Altman, recently said the company was postponing a potential public offering until 2027 as it continues efforts to strengthen its finances and pursue a much higher valuation.

For Anthropic, that could create an opportunity to enter the public markets before its larger rival. However, the company has not finalized the timing of its offering, and the plans remain subject to change.

data.title: 'Calmer heads' to start driving price discovery next week: SA analyst
data.description:
Following a week of chaotic market volatility driven by the Federal Reserve and a quarterly triple-witching event, investors can expect calmer heads to drive price discovery starting next week, according to Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research.

King anticipates that as the reactionary trading subsides, a stark divergence in sector performance will emerge looking toward the year's end. Semiconductors (SMH up 57% YTD) and the tech-heavy Nasdaq (QQQ up 17% YTD) are expected to build on their gains, while crypto (IBIT down 11% YTD) is positioned well for a turnaround.

Conversely, the SA analyst forecasts that older-economy proxies like industrials (XLI up 9% YTD) and the Dow Jones (DIA up 7% YTD) may struggle to keep pace. Bonds (SHY) (TLT) (IEF) (ZROZ), meanwhile, will "probably start to surprise to the upside."

"Next week we will see calmer heads begin the process of price discovery into year end," King said.

Meanwhile, the stock market ended mixed Friday as Treasury yields reversed Thursday's retreat, with the 10-year note (US10Y) climbing back to the key 5.0% mark.

The S&P 500 (SP500) +0.2%, the Dow (DJI) -0.2%, and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) +0.4%.

data.title: Navient completes $612.5M securitization backed by private education loans
data.description:
Navient (NAVI)  closed its $612.5M Navient Private Education Loan Trust (NAVSL) 2026-A transaction, its fourth student loan securitization this year, the company said Friday.

The deal is Navient's (NAVI) first designed to support investment by investors subject to European Union’s securitization regulation and the United Kingdom’s securitization regulatory framework.

"Expanding access to our securitizations for investors operating under EU and UK regulatory frameworks reflects our ongoing commitment to the capital markets," said Chief Financial Officer Steve Hauber.

Navient (NAVI) agreed to keep a portion of the notes and certificates on terms designed to align with the risk retention requirements of the EU securitization regulation and the UK securitization regulatory framework and support the compliance needs of investors subject to EU or UK requirements.

Navient (NAVI) stock fell 3.4% in Friday regular-hours trading.

The securitization's book runner is J.P. Morgan (JPM).
